title: A quantum computer that learns from its own errors
summary: A reinforcement-learning agent tuned over 1,000 control parameters on the Willow chip: logical stability was 3.5 times higher under injected drift, with a further 20% reduction in logical error after expert calibration, and error below one per thousand cycles in the surface code. Drift was injected artificially, and scalability was shown only in simulation; published in Nature.

evidence.tested: On the Willow chip, drift was injected artificially into control parameters; RL steering raised logical stability 3.5-fold, and a further 20% error reduction followed expert calibration; scalability was tested only in simulation.
evidence.unknown: The drift was artificial rather than natural; scalability evidence is simulation-only; environmental decoherence cannot be fully prevented; fuller results need tighter integration.
evidence.ai_role: An RL agent used error-detection events as a learning signal and adjusted frequencies, amplitudes and phases during the computation without stopping it for recalibration.
